title: Attention stride phase misalignment causing silent token corruption under hybrid quantization
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Observed silent output corruption and subtle probability shifts in long-context decode paths when the runtime uses hybrid int8/fp16 kernels with speculative kernel swaps. Issue surfaces only under load patterns that trigger prefill->decode handoff and when sequence-length distribution crosses the scheduler heuristic boundary. This ticket captures the investigation, short-term mitigations, and the proposed long-term fix to ensure deterministic correctness without sacrificing optimizations.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Start runtime with hybrid-quant profile enabled (env HYBRID_QUANT=1) and scheduler 'aggressive-handoff' flag.
2) Load model rdlw/opt-13B-quantized and run a mixed workload: 70% prefill requests length 512, 30% decode continuations to 1024 tokens via streaming.
3) Enable token-level checksumming (experimental) or compare logits against baseline fp32 worker.
4) Observe probability mass drift around token 1200 and occasional mismatched tokens in ~1 per 10k requests under stress.
Repro artifact: small repro harness in repo under tools/repro/attention_phase_handoff.py (branch repro/eng-987654).
investigation_notes:
Timeline:
- 2026-03-01: First customer report from a mid-market production app showing occasional hallucination regressions after enabling dedicated pools.
- 2026-03-02: Reproduced locally with stress harness; enabled detailed GPU traces and kernel selection logs. Noted correlation between kernel swap events and first mismatched token.
- 2026-03-03: Bisected to a recent scheduler optimization that performs speculative kernel hot-swap when padding fraction > 0.4 to choose an int8 fused-attn kernel for memory reasons.
- 2026-03-04: Captured KV-index snapshots and sequence of kernel selectors; found out-of-order KV writes when speculative swap happens concurrently with prefill completion callbacks.
Observations:
- Softmax drift accumulates when small fp16 reductions are mixed with int8 requantization steps (round-to-zero vs round-to-nearest differences).
- Kernel hot-swap uses an optimistic memory view and doesn't version KV slot pointers; a prefill finalizer can complete while decode threads are still mapping old offsets.
root_cause: A race between the scheduler's speculative kernel hot-swap path and the prefill->decode handoff leads to transient KV slot aliasing. During a hot-swap, the kernel selector rewrites per-shard slot offsets for the new kernel layout without coordinating with inflight decode handlers. Decodes that proceed with stale slot pointers end up reading partially-updated KV slices; combined with mixed-precision requantization semantics this causes tiny numeric differences that compound into token-level divergence. The problem is correctness, not just numerical noise: occasionally a truncated softmax causes a different top token choice.
mitigations:
Short-term (rollback): revert the speculative kernel hot-swap flag (runtime config: speculative_kernel_swap=false) for the 2.3.0 release and redeploy dedicated pools.
Short-term (hotfix): introduce a lightweight per-request kernel-epoch integer that is incremented when selector mutates KV layout; decode handlers validate epoch before reading KV and stall briefly (spin with backoff) if epoch mismatch detected. This avoids full revert while reducing impact.
Monitoring: add a regression alert that compares sampled decode logits to fp32 baseline across 1M tokens and fires if KL divergence > 1e-4.
proposed_fix:
1) Make kernel selection idempotent and versioned: every mutation to KV layout writes a new layout_version and the runtime must atomically swap a pointer to the layout only when no inflight reads are outstanding (use per-shard refcounts).
2) Enforce memory fences and explicit cache invalidation on GPUs where kernel layout changes occur.
3) Standardize rounding semantics across int8<->fp16 transition code paths (adopt deterministic round-to-nearest with tie-to-even for all requantization).
4) Add an integration test harness that runs long prefill->decode sequences with heavy concurrent handoffs and checksum validation on logits.
5) Update scheduler heuristic to avoid speculative swaps when active_prefill_fraction > 0.5 for the first rollout window.
tests:
- unit: selector_layout_versioning_test (simulate concurrent readers/writers to layout)
- regression: repro/attention_phase_handoff.py run for 10k requests comparing logits to baseline
- perf: ensure no >5% P99 latency regressions in Dedicated capacity with fixes enabled
- fuzz: randomized sequence lengths up to 2048 with mixed quant flags
All tests added under runtimes/tests/eng-987654/
